narr: A broad area of low pressure across the Great Lakes region stalled out well to the west of the region early on Sunday, April 30th. A secondary area of low pressure developed and moved up the Eastern Seaboard and tracked across interior New England from Sunday, April 30th through Monday, May 1st. Widespread heavy rainfall occurred, and flooding was enhanced for this weather event due to the seasonal timing of the rains with spring soils being high in moisture and vegetation still being dormant. These two factors lead to increased run-off. Rain started across southern and coastal areas early on Sunday April 30th, with the heaviest rainfall Sunday night into early Monday morning. The rainfall on Sunday produced limited flooding, but set the stage for what was to come by swelling rivers and filling ditches ahead of the heavier rain. Heavy rain started around 3 AM and continued through 10 AM Monday with rainfall rates between 1 to 1.5 inches an hour. This caused flooding to rapidly develop, resulting in widespread flash flooding. The rainfall ended by midday on Monday May 1st. Runoff spilled into tributary rivers and major rivers that led to ongoing flooding for the next several days with most rivers cresting late on Monday May 1st or on May 2nd. Public infrastructure impacts were widespread for the event with over $4.2 million in damage. Oxford and Androscoggin Counties reported the most monetary damage to roads for the event. ||Another aspect of the system was a period of strong gusty winds Sunday night that started along the coastline and extended inland causing localized power outages and tree damage. Wind gusts of 50 mph were recorded at the Portland Jetport, and gusts to near 50 mph were also recorded inland. Strongest wind gusts up to 65 mph were reported across the Mid-coast region. Power outages were reported due to a few downed trees and numerous snapped tree limbs.
ev: Heavy rainfall between 3.5 and 4.5 inches on already saturated ground resulted in a washout on Maine Route 108.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Maine Route 156 in Weld.
Rounds of heavy rainfall resulted in flooding of small streams in Washington. The Little Medomack Brook washout out part of Calderwood Road and Davis Stream flooded Varner road.
Runoff from Hemingway Ridge caused the Swift Cambridge River to flood and close the major access Route 26, leading to significant disruption to travel in and out of the region.
Heavy rainfall of 3.5 to 4.5 inches on the morning of May 1 resulted in a washout on South Rumford Road.
Significant damage to Spring Run Hill Road in Edgecomb after an un-named tributary to the Deer Meadow Brook flooded 325 feet of roadway. Multiple Culverts and 175 feet of roadway washed out.
Heavy rainfall caused the Swift River to rapidly rise and washout on Roxbury Notch Road.

Heay rainfall resulted in numerous road closures and washouts across Brownfield including Sam Brown Hill Road, Hampshire Road, Merrill Corner Road and Dugway Road. There were numerous washouts on Old County Road.
Washout on Mount Micha Road after approximately 4 inches of rain fell on already saturated ground on the morning of May 1.
Multiple washouts between Gore Road and Hidden Lake Road on the morning of May 1 after 3.5 to 4.5 inches of rain fell over already saturated ground.

Heavy rain estimated around 3.5 inches cause an un-named small stream to the Fish Brook to overwhelm a culvert on Green Road in Fairfield. The resulting flood washed out a 10 foot section of the road.
Washout occurred on Rabbit Valley Road in Otisfield after 3.5 to 4.5 inches of rain fell on saturated ground early in the morning of May 1.
Heavy rainfall estimated between 3.5 to 4.5 inches on the morning of May 1 resulted in a washout on Webbs Mills Road.

Multiple washouts on College Road train tracks flooding and again near the Stetson Brook crossing. Multiple washouts on Lane Road from an un-named stream that flows into Stetson Brook. Road washouts on both South and North Mountain Roads. Road washed away on Morse Cemetary Road after an un-named stream overwhelmed a culvert. Damage to bridge on South Mountain Road.
Flash floods caused a washout on Greenwoods Road after 3.5 to 4.5 inches of rainfall fell on the morning of May 1.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches fell over saturated ground on the morning of May 1. The runoff caused a washout on Waterford Road.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches fell over already saturated ground on the morning of May 1. The resultant flash flood washed out a portion of Route 160.
Multiple washouts on Carsley Road in Harrison.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches over already saturated ground resulted in a washout on Route 117 in Denmark.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches fell over already saturated ground resulting in a 4 foot sinkhole on Smith Road.

Flash flooding caused washouts on multiple roads in the town of Industry. Those roads include Greenwood Brook Road, Shaw Hill Road, New Sharon Road, Baily Road with multiple washouts, and Federal Row.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches caused a washout on Route 5 in Lovell.
Town of Hartford sustained a washout between Route 219 and 140 and damage to two bridges.
Heavy rainfall between 3.5 to 4.5 inches caused flooding on Stow Road or Maine Route 113 resulting in a water rescue.
Flooding of the Darnit Brook damaged Rosenburg and Decoster Roads in Sumner. Decoster Road sustained multiple washouts near the brook crossing and two of five culvers.
River Road washed out by excessive runoff from 5.0 to 5.5 inches of rainfall on the morning of May 1. Road impassable for over a month.
Flooding on North Road in Gilead resulted in a water rescue to a motorist.
Flash flooding caused numerous shoulder washouts on roads across West Paris. The hardest hit road was along Ellingwood Road near Ryerson Hill Road where a complete washout occurred.
A water rescue was needed around Route 17 in North Jay/Wilton town line for a car washed off the road.
Heavy rain resulted in a washout on Gibson Road in West Bethel.
Flash flooding caused washouts on numerous roads in Woodstock including Redding Road, Concord Road, Pond Road, and Swinton Road.
West Branch of the Nezinscot River flooded Redding Road Bridge.

Heavy rainfall between 3 and 4 inches fell over Dixfield on the morning of May 1. The heavy rain over saturated ground caused a washout on Averill Hill Road. Severy Hill and Valley Road were closed due to flooding. Route 164 and Coolidge Road had multiple washouts along the edge of the road. A significant washout occurred on Valley Brook Road.
Heavy rainfall resulted in excessive runoff and a rapid rise in the Sunday River. A vehicle was stuck in flood waters and necessitated a water rescue on Sunday River Road.
Bridge washout on Fern Road in Lovell from the Kezar River.
Runoff from Jim Hill in Norway flooded and resulted in the closure of Route 118.
